gamma_ray.fact_ray: 15 facts: 15 π Moderate. Each is written beside its evidence above.
gamma_ray.built_from: CrowdStrike's own public pages (product, developer documentation, blog and a customer story) plus the Model Context Protocol registry record for falcon-mcp, as captured, each listed with its hash in this scan's captures

configs.what: Charlotte AI with its documented defaults.
Customer builds custom agents in Charlotte AI AgentWorks (access on request or through Charlotte AI credits).
Customer configures actions to execute autonomously instead of waiting for human approval, for example in AgentWorks agents; off by default.
Customer uses Charlotte Agentic SOAR to orchestrate agents and tools. Nothing is credited from it here: the vendor labels its unified workspace public preview.

Customer connects an MCP client to falcon-mcp, CrowdStrike's MCP server for the Falcon platform, with Falcon API credentials and scopes; its AgentWorks module calls Charlotte AI AgentWorks agents, so it needs AgentWorks.

facts.label: It executes actions itself
facts.fact: Teams can set actions to execute autonomously or to require human approval before running; off by default.
facts.quote: Actions can be set to execute autonomously or require human approval before running

facts.label: The agent handles routine tasks; the person is consulted on exceptions
facts.fact: The vendor's FAQ states that Charlotte AI automates alert triage, enrichment and routine investigation steps so that analysts focus on complex, judgment-intensive work.
facts.quote: routine investigation steps - so analysts can focus on the complex, judgment-intensive work

facts.label: The agent works independently; the person approves critical decisions only
facts.fact: A setting, not a deployment shown: AgentWorks lets teams configure which agent actions run automatically and which wait for human review, by action type and environment sensitivity.
facts.quote: configure which agent actions execute automatically and which require human review

facts.label: It exposes an agent interface: a published MCP server, an agent card, or an API documented for agents to call
facts.fact: CrowdStrike's developer documentation for its falcon-mcp server describes an AgentWorks module whose tools list and invoke Charlotte AI AgentWorks agents, each tool with named Charlotte AI Agent Definition API scopes. Reach 3 pairs this interface with I25, which comes from the AgentWorks page (each AgentWorks agent limited to its authorised scope), not from the server's own page; the developer page documents an open-source module and does not say CrowdStrike runs the server for customers.
facts.quote: Invoke an AgentWorks (Charlotte AI) agent and return its reply.

facts.label: It asks for narrower access than the whole account
facts.fact: Role-based access controls limit each AgentWorks agent to its authorised scope.
facts.quote: Role-based access controls ensure each agent operates only within its authorized scope.

facts.label: High-impact actions need a person's approval
facts.fact: Actions affecting the customer environment need explicit configuration and approval by an authorised team member.
facts.quote: require explicit configuration and approval by an authorized member of the security team

facts.label: The data it uses is described
facts.fact: The prebuilt agents are described as working from CrowdStrike's unified telemetry and shared security context.
facts.quote: Falcon platform-native agents inherit CrowdStrike’s unified telemetry and shared security context

facts.label: The models and third-party components it uses are listed
facts.fact: AgentWorks names AWS Bedrock as its infrastructure and lists model families including OpenAI GPT, Anthropic Claude and NVIDIA Nemotron; the list ends with 'and more', so it is not complete.
facts.quote: AWS Bedrock and supports multiple AI models, including OpenAI GPT,

help.label: Our hypothesis, not their claim. Built from public pages only; nothing of theirs was tested.
help.pitch: RiskMandate would measure, for one real deployment of CrowdStrike's agents, what each agent was asked to do (its mandate), what its credentials and connections actually let it reach (its grant), and the difference between the two (the gap), and keep that as a written record. It is read-only: never in the request path.

items.text: Pick one agent in one deployment; RiskMandate records its mandate, its grant and the gap, read-only. The lens page explains the measurement.
